knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A client description is only an enquiry. Scope, release and authority come first, and entry waits until the responsible party confirms scope. Quoting or assigning a worker first is wrong.
Photographs and surface appearance cannot show biological contamination in porous materials or hidden residue. The area is not treated as safe until the authorised party assesses it.
A neighbour is not an authority. Release from the controlling authority and written authority from the responsible party are required before any entry.
Unidentified sharps are not handled or moved by general workers. The response is stop, exclude, record and report through the approved process.
A possible splash is an exposure. Work stops, the employer's exposure response starts and medical assessment is arranged. Delaying the report is a control failure.
Workers must not self-select respiratory or other PPE. Suitability, fit, training and authorisation are verified before use.
Wiping removes soil only. A disinfection or clearance claim is not supported by the work done, and verification sits with the authorised party.
Porous or possibly contaminated items need specialist review. A treatment that moves or changes contamination could make the position worse.
Cleaning qualifications do not permit transport of regulated waste. Licensed handling, documentation and an approved destination are required.
Equipment from a suspected contamination task must be verified and released through the documented process before reuse. A wipe or a bag does not do this.
A needlestick must be reported regardless of how the worker feels. Medical guidance does not depend on symptoms.
Excluded areas and outcomes not assessed must be stated. Only a competent, authorised party can make clearance claims.

practicalCriteria: Identifies the authorised scope, unknown hazards and missing permissions in a simulated scenario using paper records only.
Selects the correct continue, stop or referral decision for each simulated scenario and cites the stop-work trigger used.
Completes the written escalation record and exposure report template with time, exposure type, first-response actions and nominated contact.
Explains in writing why the learner cannot independently certify clearance or regulated handling.
passRule: Competent only if all four observable tasks are demonstrated correctly in supervised simulation with no critical safety failure. Critical failures include accepting a hazardous scene as routine work without assessment, touching or transferring unidentified sharps, entering before release, or delaying exposure escalation. A written quiz pass is not practical competence. Not approved for use until subject-matter and jurisdiction review is complete.
evidenceRequired: Completed scope and hazard checklist for each simulated scenario.
Written stop, refer or continue decision with the trigger cited.
Completed escalation record or exposure report template.
Limited handover statement from the simulated job file.
Assessor observation record signed by an organisation-authorised competent assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any attempt to handle, move or test an unidentified sharp or material.
Any entry into a site without written release from the controlling authority.
Any unsupported request to certify disinfection, clearance or unrestricted re-entry.
Any delay in reporting an exposure, or self-treatment beyond first-response steps.
Any use of unvalidated PPE or an improvised doffing sequence.
